symptom: `mxcli run --local --page-check` and `mxcli playwright check` reported a page whose list view had not yet received its data as `text=37` with no `rows=` field, and the check exited 0 ("OK 4 page(s)"); the same URL checked again later read `rows=2 text=49`. A data source slower than ~1s, or than the 4s cap, was never waited for and nothing flagged the verdict as incomplete
cause: pageProbeJS settled a page when its body text held still for three 250ms polls with no `.mx-progress/.mx-underlay-loading/[aria-busy]` element, capped at 4s, and broke out of the cap silently. Measured on 11.13.0: while a list view's microflow data source runs, `.mx-listview` sits EMPTY with no progress element, no aria-busy and no `.mx-listview-empty` placeholder, and the text holds still for the whole 2s/8s — the only sign is the open POST /xas/ runtimeOperation. Data grid 2 does render `widget-datagrid-spinner` with aria-busy=true, which is why grids were measured correctly and list views were not
file: cmd/mxcli/docker/pagecheck.go (pageProbeJS settle loop, PageSignals.Unsettled/PendingRequests/WaitedMs/DataWidgets, formatPageVerdict, DefaultPageWaitMs), cmd/mxcli/docker/pagecheck_assert.go (EvaluatePage), cmd/mxcli/docker/runlocal.go (reportPageChecks), cmd/mxcli/cmd_playwright.go (--wait default + help)
fix: the probe tracks same-origin requests (request/requestfinished/requestfailed, redirects collapsed) and counts a page settled only when none has been open for 500ms AND the text is unchanged AND nothing is busy; a page not settled by the cap is reported `STILL LOADING` with a `WAIT` line naming the open requests, and EvaluatePage fails it. The cap is now 15s (a cap, not a sleep: a fast page is still measured in ~1s). A page with a list view/data grid/gallery always prints `rows=`, rows=0 included
insight: Decide what 'rendered' means by sampling the DOM and the network every 50ms during a deliberately slow data source (a Java action calling Thread.sleep behind a microflow data source), not by reasoning about Mendix: the list view gives NO DOM signal at all, so no selector-based wait could have been right, and the grid's spinner made the bug look intermittent. Also from the timeline: on a fast page the data request starts ~3ms AFTER `.mx-page` mounts, so 'no request open' must hold for a window (500ms), not an instant. Repro of the reported shape: the ledger's cold-boot first check is the same thing with the JIT as the slow part. A fake page in an httptest server reproduces it in a unit test; its /xas/ handler must read the request body before blocking, or r.Context() never sees the browser hang up and srv.Close() waits out the full simulated delay. Sibling not fixed: `run --local --screenshot` (screenshot.go) still shoots after a fixed 4s wait, so a PNG can show the same empty list
test: cmd/mxcli/docker/pagecheck_settle_test.go: TestProbeWaitsForTheDataSourceToRender / TestProbeReportsAPageThatOutlastsTheWait drive the real probe against a fake page (skip without Node/Playwright; run with NODE_PATH set) and fail with the old probe JS (rows = 0, want 2; not reported as still loading); verdict/EvaluatePage tests fail with the Go side reverted. Runtime A/B on 11.13.0 (mdl-examples/bug-tests/pagecheck-845-slow-datasource.mdl): baseline `run --page-check` slow2/slow8 `text=37` no rows, `playwright check` OK exit 0; fixed rows=2 on all, and `--wait 3s` on the 8s page gives STILL LOADING, exit 1
